idiom_name: fine-grained reactive signals (Leptos/Dioxus) with closures in the view; no observable view-model class
implementation_notes: Rust has no MVVM runtime, and ownership makes the classic graph hostile: a view-model holding observers that hold the view is a reference cycle (Rc<RefCell<...>> leaks) and callbacks must be 'static. The idiomatic replacement is fine-grained signals: in Leptos, signal(0) returns a getter/setter pair whose reads inside a closure placed in view! are tracked, so only the affected node updates, and set_count.set(...) is the command; Dioxus offers the same model. Where a team prefers message-driven updates, iced's Elm architecture (Message enum, update, view) is the alternative - a different pattern family, not a variant of this one. Hand-rolled Rc<RefCell<Observed>> view-models are where Rust MVVM attempts usually go wrong.
pitfalls: Signals are Copy handles with 'static lifetimes: .get() clones the value - keep large state in a store or inside Rc and read it with .with().
Only signals and closures are reactive in a view! macro: writing {user.get()} renders once and never updates.
Hand-written observer graphs with Rc<RefCell<...>> leak cycles and panic at run time when borrowed across callbacks; prefer signal/store types.
Reactive ownership is explicit: spawned tasks or subscriptions that outlive the component lose their reactive scope and silently stop updating the view.
